messages:
pagerduty-bot: PAGER: P-2026 - KV cache & continuous-batching surge (sev: 2). Multiple model variants (Llama-3-14B, Mistral-7B MQA) showing rapid KV growth and batch queue pressure. Page routed to infra-oncall. https://pagerduty.local/incidents/P-2026

sara: acknowledging, taking lead. I'm seeing 10x increase in prefix cardinality and KV writes. Continuous-batching queue length spiked to ~6k across eu clusters, backpressure causing p99 generation to jump.

ops-bot: metrics -> https://metrics.redwood/internal/d/kv/contbatch?var-cluster=eu-1 (seen: kv_evictions/sec = 18k, contbatch_queue_depth = 6200, p99_gen_latency = 1.8s)

mike: are customer-facing 5xxs or degraded responses? any errors logged?

sara: yes, ~0.8% 503s on hostpool-eu-A for model=llama-3-14b-qa-variant over last 5m. Error traces show "kv cache OOM" and generation timeouts. Also costs are spiking due to repeated miss->recompute.

devon: initial theory: a sudden influx of high-cardinality prefixes (short-chat + system messages) broke the prefix-based KV cache heuristics, combined with continuous-batching holding large pending requests causing KV store amplification. Two quick mitigations: 1) disable continuous-batching for suspect model variants, 2) tighten batching window / token caps.

irene: +1 for model-scoped disabling. Also bump kv idle eviction to aggressively evict thinly-used prefixes. We can flip without full restart. Suggest values: "cont_batch.enabled": false (model scope), "batch.max_wait_ms": 8, "batch.max_batch_tokens": 1024, "kv.idle_eviction_ms": 30000.

sara: preparing hotfix patch now. plan: apply model-level runtime override for llama-3-14b-qa-variant and mistral-7b-mqa-variant to disable cont-batch; adjust global batch params as stopgap. Will route new requests to fallback variants if latency > 1s.

sara: running command to stage config for clusters eu-1/eu-2:

```
redwoodctl config set --scope model:llama-3-14b-qa-variant \
  --patch '{"continuous_batching": {"enabled": false}, "batching": {"max_wait_ms": 8, "max_batch_tokens": 1024}}' \
  --clusters eu-1,eu-2 --author sara --note "mitigate kv-contbatch blowup"
```

ops-bot: submitted config patch, id=cfg-7842. Applying to shards 10-15 on eu-1.

deploy-bot: hotfix deployment started -> deploy-2026-08-09-7842. Rolling to shard 10..15 (eu-1). Logs: https://deploys.redwood/internal/deploys/deploy-2026-08-09-7842

sara: also toggled kv idle eviction parameter on runtime for affected hosts:

```
redwoodctl runtime set --cluster eu-1 --key kv.idle_eviction_ms --value 30000
```

mike: can we also temporarily route heavy-entropy prefixes to lower-capacity fallback models? e.g., route MQA calls to a dedicated MQA-optimized pool. That would reduce cross-model kv amplification.

devon: good call. I can flip routing rules for the next hour: set policy to prefer dedicated-mqa-pool for requests flagged with "mqa:true". Command: `redwoodctl route update --policy mqa_fallback --priority high`

ops-bot: patch applied. routing rule mqa_fallback active (effective ~30s).

ops-bot: live metrics update -> kv_evictions/sec down to 4.6k, contbatch_queue_depth 1.2k, p99_gen_latency 420ms (from 1.8s). Error rate on hostpool-eu-A down to 0.12%.

sara: good signal. continuing to monitor for 20m. Starting customer impact assessment.

cs-bot: customers flagged with alerts: "AcmeAnalytics" and "ScribeAI" saw increased tail latencies and intermittent 5xxs between 09:04-09:12 UTC. Draft message: "We're investigating an infrastructure-level latency issue affecting some generation requests for Llama/Mistral variants. We've applied mitigations and are monitoring. We'll follow up with timeline and root cause." Want me to send?

mike: send with note that a hotfix was applied and that we routed MQA to dedicated pool to limit blast radius. Offer to open a support call.

cs-bot: sending now (ticket links included).

devon: quick postmortem notes to capture: root cause likely spike in prefix-cardinality due to a customer A/B test producing high-variance prompts plus a release that relaxed prefix deduping heuristics last week. Fixes: revert dedupe relax, add circuit-breaker: disable cont-batch when contbatch_queue_depth > 1000 or kv_evictions/sec > 2000 for model scope. I'll open PR for runtime rule.

sara: rolling handoff now. devon will take the on-call. Summary: hotfix applied disabling cont-batch for two variants, kv idle eviction more aggressive, routing changed to dedicated MQA pool. Monitoring shows metrics improving but still slightly elevated. Active tasks: devon to prepare durable rollback & PR, irene to tune eviction thresholds, mike to validate customer telemetry.

devon: ack, taking on-call. I'll be available for the next 4 hours, will coordinate handover notes and start PR now. ```
